vignette: 62-year-old woman with 24-hour ambulatory monitoring showing daytime average 158/96 mm Hg. On lifestyle modification and stable maximally tolerated doses of four antihypertensives (including a diuretic and spironolactone) for 4 months, with adherence confirmed by pharmacy refill records and pill counts. Screening was negative for primary aldosteronism (normal aldosterone-renin ratio), obstructive sleep apnea (home sleep test), and drug- or alcohol-induced hypertension. Her primary care physician has co-managed her blood pressure for 14 months with five encounters, four in person. The planned FDA market-authorized RDN device will be used per its labeled indication. The patient will be enrolled in a CMS-approved CED study. The operator is an interventional cardiologist with active endovascular experience who completed five proctored cases with this device; the facility runs a hypertension program with a hypertension navigator and specialist access, has CT angiography, and a cardiac catheterization lab. Referral is by the primary care physician who manages the patient's hypertension longitudinally. Renal CT angiography shows anatomy suitable for RDN and there are no contraindications in the device labeling. No prior RDN.
